paragraphs.en: Fill one of the 28 spaces each turn. Press Enter to roll five dice. You can record the roll or reroll selected dice up to twice. If the roll fails to qualify for the chosen row, enter zero.

In Fours, Fives and Sixes, sum only the dice showing the named value. Chance takes the sum of all five dice. A straight is five consecutive values, and a full house is three of one value and two of another. Both score the sum of all five dice. Five equal dice score 50 in Balut regardless of their value. If Balut is full, five sixes can still score 30 in Sixes or Chance.

You earn two points for each of these row totals you reach: 52 in Fours, 65 in Fives, 78 in Sixes and 100 in Chance. Four straights earn four points, four full houses earn three and each Balut earns two. Add up all entries. Below 300, subtract two points. At 300–349, subtract one. At 350–399, make no adjustment. Starting at 400, add one point for each 50 above 350, up to six at 650. The highest final score wins. The maximum is 29 points.

Use the number keys to select dice by face value and Space to hear them. Enter rolls selected dice or opens the score sheet when none are selected. After the third roll, Enter opens the sheet. B also opens it. Use Up and Down to change rows and Left and Right to move between cells. After rolling, move to the scoring cell of a row with space and press Enter. Escape closes the sheet. S reads game points and Shift+S reads the raw total. Both are in the last row.
